1 · Intro

When to use it.

Most transactions you submit in Oracle HCM do not take effect right away. They route to approvers, and each approver sees a task in their notifications or worklist.

Knowing where to look, and what withdraw and send back do, keeps transactions from stalling before payroll cutoff.

Use this whenYou submitted a transaction and need to know where it is, or a task has landed on your worklist.

2 · Walk through

Step by step.

Follow along in Oracle HCM. Check off each step as you go.

Watch-outs

  • Check the bell daily, and before every payroll cutoff. A transaction waiting on an approver is not in payroll yet.
  • Rejecting means the whole approval chain starts over after resubmission; send back or request information when a small fix is all that is needed.
  • Open item: confirm Vanderbilt's approval chains by transaction type, whether delegation is enabled for HCMs, and the exact action labels on screen.

Official documentation

Vendor documentation describes the standard process. Vanderbilt's setup, codes, and rules in this course take priority.

HCM Workflow and Worklists

Use when: You submitted a transaction and need to know where it is, or a task has landed on your worklist. · System: Oracle HCM

  1. Open the notifications bell at the top of Oracle.
  2. Find a transaction you submitted and check its status.
  3. Act on tasks assigned to you.
  4. Use Request More Information or send back instead of rejecting for small fixes.
  5. Withdraw your own transaction if you need to change it.
    • Withdraw is on by default in Oracle; your configuration may differ.
  6. Set up delegation before you are out.

Watch-outs

  • Check the bell daily, and before every payroll cutoff. A transaction waiting on an approver is not in payroll yet.
  • Rejecting means the whole approval chain starts over after resubmission; send back or request information when a small fix is all that is needed.
  • Open item: confirm Vanderbilt's approval chains by transaction type, whether delegation is enabled for HCMs, and the exact action labels on screen.
